title: The Wild Choir
premise: Mirabel Sandoval, a beast-speaker concealing her forbidden gift while keeping ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things, inherits a dying stranger's map to the Hollow Choir — a broken covenant between the human realm and the wild places that once sang in harmony. Hunted by the Guild's enforcers and guided by a sarcastic marsh-fox and a disgraced covenant-warden named Emeric, she must gather the scattered voices of the old pact before the solstice, when the silence between realms becomes permanent. The final voice turns out to be Mirabel's own mother, long believed dead and bound as the covenant's failing anchor. In the end, Mirabel sacrifices her hidden gift itself to reforge the choir, choosing open belonging over secret power, and wins both realms and Emeric's love.
about_author: Mirabel Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk songs in coastal villages before turning to fiction. She writes by lamplight in a drafty house full of rescued animals who, she insists, talk back.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. In the Guild's counting house, Mirabel balances accounts for griffin feathers and bottled thunder while hiding her ability to hear animals speak. A caged songbird begs her for help, and she nearly answers aloud. Emotional beat: the ache of concealment, belonging withheld from oneself.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A bleeding stranger collapses into the Guild's back entrance, presses a bone map into Mirabel's hands, and whispers 'the Choir is starving' before dying. Guild enforcers arrive asking questions she can't answer. Emotional beat: fear igniting into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Rats Overheard
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Using her gift in secret, Mirabel questions the warehouse rats and learns the Guild has been buying up covenant-relics for years — deliberately silencing the wild. She decides to flee with the map. Emotional beat: first act of open defiance.

chapters.title: The Marsh Fox Bargains
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Pursued into the fens, she is cornered by a talking marsh-fox named Quillfeather who offers guidance in exchange for a debt unnamed. Their uneasy alliance begins. Emotional beat: wary humor masking loneliness on both sides.

chapters.title: Emeric of the Broken Order
chapters.summary: POV Emeric. A disgraced covenant-warden intercepts Mirabel, intending to take the map to his superiors; instead he finds his old order complicit in the silence. He defects, badly. Emotional beat: duty cracking against conscience.

chapters.title: Three Voices in the Well
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The trio reaches the first waypoint, a drowned village where three covenant voices linger in a well. Mirabel coaxes them free, but the effort reveals how much of her gift each use costs. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Guild Closes Its Hand
chapters.summary: POV Emeric. Guild hunters burn the safe roads behind them; an old friend of Emeric's leads the pursuit and offers him reinstatement if he betrays Mirabel. He refuses and takes a wound doing it. Emotional beat: loyalty proven at cost.

chapters.title: Songs the Mountains Kept
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. High in the Ashspine, they find a hermit choir of stone-giants still humming fragments of the covenant. One giant recognizes the map's maker — and says he was Mirabel's father's friend. Emotional beat: grief surfacing, family mystery opened.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Name in Stone
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The giants reveal that Mirabel's mother did not die — she was taken as the covenant's living anchor when it began to fail. Mirabel reels; Emeric steadies her. Emotional beat: hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Quillfeather's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Quillfeather. The fox's unnamed debt comes due: he was once a human chorister transformed as punishment, and he needs Mirabel to speak his true name at the reforging or vanish forever. Emotional beat: vulnerability beneath sardonic armor.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot How to Listen
chapters.summary: POV Emeric. The trio infiltrates the capital, where bells are being melted and birds caged on Guild orders. They witness the machinery of enforced silence firsthand. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: An Offer Wearing a Friend's Face
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The Guild's master, Serane Voss, captures them — not to kill, but to recruit: she claims the silence protects humanity from the wild's hunger, and shows Mirabel a memory of what the old covenant once devoured. Emotional beat: certainty shaken.

chapters.title: The Cell Beneath the Bells
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Imprisoned, Mirabel discovers the prison walls themselves are made of pressed songbirds' bones. With the rats of the city answering her call, she engineers an escape. Emotional beat: despair transmuted into cunning.

chapters.title: What Voss Showed Was True
chapters.summary: POV Emeric. Fugitive again, Emeric researches Voss's claim in a forbidden archive and confirms a partial truth: one voice of the covenant did turn ravenous — and it may be the anchor herself. Emotional beat: dread of what saving the world might require.

chapters.title: The Drowned Choir Rises
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At the sunken cathedral waypoint, the gathered voices converge, but the Guild ambushes them. Quillfeather is gravely wounded holding the line. Emotional beat: love declared in crisis — Mirabel and Emeric finally admit what they are to each other.

chapters.title: Nineteen Voices, Two Missing
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Counting the recovered voices, two remain: the traitor-voice and the anchor. The solstice is three days away. Mirabel realizes the final voice must be given freely, not taken. Emotional beat: quiet determination before the storm.

chapters.title: The Anchor at World's Edge
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At the covenant's root-tree, Mirabel finds her mother — half-rooted, half-song, barely remembering her own name. Their reunion is tender and terrible: her mother begs to be released even if it unmakes the pact. Emotional beat: love against duty in its purest form.

chapters.title: Serane Voss Comes to Sing
chapters.summary: POV Emeric. Voss arrives with her army, but not to destroy the ritual — to seize the anchor's power for the Guild. Emeric holds the tree-line alone so Mirabel can sing. Emotional beat: sacrifice without spectacle.

chapters.title: The Voice That Turned
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mid-reforging, the ravenous voice manifests through her mother's fading form, and Mirabel must face it: it is every promise humans broke, given appetite. She answers not with force but with the ledger — reading aloud every impossible thing the wild ever gave freely. Emotional beat: reconciliation through honest accounting.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken True
chapters.summary: POV Quillfeather. At the climax, Mirabel speaks the fox's forgotten name; he stands human for one breath, chooses to remain a fox, and joins the choir willingly. The covenant reforges around twenty-one voices — and reaches for a twenty-second. Emotional beat: transformation accepted, identity chosen.

chapters.title: The Twenty-Second Voice
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The covenant demands a living speaker to bind it, and only Mirabel's hidden gift will do. She gives it up entirely — pouring her beast-speech into the pact — and the realms knit together in a single vast chord as Voss's power crumbles. Emotional beat: the climactic cost paid in full.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Counting
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Weeks later, Mirabel keeps ledgers again — but now the Guild trades openly with the wild, her mother rests healed under the root-tree, and though she can no longer hear animals speak, Quillfeather stays anyway, translating. Emeric asks her to stay. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, love answered, silence turned to song.
